newsitem.title: INDIA: India Hind Lever denies insider trading.
newsitem.headline: India Hind Lever denies insider trading.

text.p: India's Hindustan Lever Ltd on Tuesday denied newspaper reports that it had indulged in insider trading.

Leading financial newspapers reproted that market regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is investigating an alleged case of insider trading by Anglo-Dutch conglomerate Unilever Plc's Indian subsidiary.
"There is no substance to the allegation," a company spokesman told Reuters on Tuesday. "There is no insider trading. We can prove it and we'll respond to SEBI."
The spokesman said the company planned to issue an official statement on the allegation later on Tuesday.

The Economic Times said SEBI had issued an official notice to the chairman and directors to explain their position on the alleged insider trading in Brooke Bond Lipton India Ltd (BBIL) shares prior to its merger with Hindustan Lever.
L.K. Singhvi, SEBI executive director, told the Economic Times Hindustan Lever has been given two weeks to explain.
"SEBI has discovered that HLL bought about eight lakh (800,000) shares of BBIL some two weeks prior to the announcement in April 1996 of the merger," it said.
Hindustan Lever is the largest multinational operating in India. Its shares are included in the benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange.
